IsAllowedAtNeow.rationale: Kaleidoscope.cs:24-31 is `base.IsAllowedAtNeow(player) && player.UnlockState.CharacterCardPools.Count() == ModelDb.AllCharacters.Count()`. The predicate is FALSE for the sim's unlock state, not merely unmodelled: the sim has exactly ONE character card pool (cards/pool.py's IRONCLAD_POOL, plus the character-agnostic Colorless and Curse pools) against the game's five characters, so the equality can never hold. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b07.py kaleido-neow): is_allowed_at_neow=False, 1 character pool of 85 cards vs ModelDb.AllCharacters = 5. This CONFIRMS .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md Sweep B's finding that kaleidoscope 'matches' -- and it is the only one of the sweep's 22 IsAllowed*/IsAllowedAtNeow overrides that does. Note the contrast the sweep flags for lasting_candy ('the sim assumes full unlocks'): that assumption does NOT make this value wrong, because the sim's missing pools are missing content, not missing unlocks. Rule 7: cards/pool.py and the sweeps file are not hashed by this record.

AfterObtained.maps_to: no counterpart; the port is a documented stub (kaleidoscope.py:8-12)
AfterObtained.rationale: Kaleidoscope.cs:33-50 builds CardsVar(2) = 2 CardRewards, each of 3 cards drawn from three OTHER characters' card pools (`Where(p => p != base.Owner.Character.CardPool)`), and offers them via RewardsCmd.OfferCustom. Waived under the shared contract's explicit 'characters other than Ironclad' exclusion -- the effect is not merely unreachable, its entire content domain (Silent/Defect/Regent/Necrobinder card pools) is outside the sim's scope by design, exactly like the orb machinery hook_dispatch guard N7 waives. This is NOT the 'the sim has no such system' shape binding rule 1 forbids waiving: the sim HAS a card-reward system (rewards.py) and a working after_obtained dispatch (run.py:552, the premise Sweep C proves live for every other stub) -- what it does not have, and will not have while it is Ironclad-only, is the cards. EXECUTED (probe kaleido-neow): add_relic('kaleidoscope') leaves the deck unchanged at 10, which is the correct no-op given there is nothing to offer. Because IsAllowedAtNeow already blocks the ONLY ported grant path (events/neow.py, the sole non-vocab reference to the id -- executed by probe `pool`), no ported run can reach this hook at all. Rule 7: rewards.py, run.py and events/neow.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: `StableShuffle(base.Owner.RunState.Rng.Niche)` (Kaleidoscope.cs:40) -- a NAMED RNG stream the port never touches (PROMPT.md bug class 16, second half)
guards.rationale: Class 16 says to check whether the stream is CONSUMED, not whether it is named -- and here it is genuinely consumed: StableShuffle over the other characters' pools draws from Rng.Niche once per reward loop iteration, so a run that takes Kaleidoscope in the real game advances Niche twice. The sim draws nothing. Carried by the same waiver as the AfterObtained hook rather than filed as a separate RNG gap, because the draw is a function of the other characters' pool LIST -- there is nothing to shuffle in an Ironclad-only sim, so no stream position can be reconstructed even in principle. It is not a latent parity bug that a fix could close in isolation: it closes only when other characters are ported. Recorded so the eventual multi-character port knows the stream is Niche and the count is 2.

guards.what: N2: `CardRarityOddsType.RegularEncounter` for the offered cards and `CardCreationOptions.ForNonCombatWithDefaultOdds(Array.Empty<CardModel>())` for the reroll options (Kaleidoscope.cs:36, 44), plus CardCreationFlags.NoCardPoolModifications
guards.rationale: Same scope as the hook: these are the odds and flags for generating other characters' cards. Recorded rather than skipped so the multi-character port has the exact options set, and because NoCardPoolModifications is the flag that stops the egg relics and other card-reward modifiers touching these three cards -- a detail that would otherwise be lost. Contrast relic/hefty_tablet in this batch, which does NOT set that flag and whose port drops the resulting hook.

RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
